subject: CardioSentry private deployment: on-prem handoff & ops playlist
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cardiosentry.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Eng Team <ops@cardiosentry.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy prep — network details and constraints

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Were ready to move forward with the private / on-prem package for our processing cluster. A few things from our side we need aligned before the install team arrives: 

- VPC peering vs. PrivateLink: we prefer direct VPC peering for low latency, but our security team wants to confirm all IP ranges and whether NAT/egress will be required.
- Private endpoints: we need certificate rotation details, expected DNS names, and whether we can host the endpoint behind our ALB.
- HSM/KMS: we will use our HSM for root key material; need the integration pattern and any operator actions required.
- Maintenance windows: propose a weekday night window (US-PST) for the initial cutover; need Redwoods expected downtime and rollback procedure.

Attached is a rough network diagram and our internal firewall template. Can your team provide a target checklist and who will own the runbook during the first two weeks of onboarding?

--
Tom Ellis
Director, Infrastructure
CardioSentry Inc.
ops@cardiosentry.com

---
Attachment(s): cardiosentry-network-diagram-v1.pdf, firewall-rule-template.txt
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@cardiosentry.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy prep — network details and constraints

Tom,

Appreciate the clear ask and the diagram — that helps a lot. High level answers and proposed owners below; Ill loop in Marissa (onprem lead) and Ben (network / peering) for technical detail and the formal checklist.

Summary answers:
- We support both VPC peering and PrivateLink. For low-latency streaming inference VPC peering is common; PrivateLink can be used where you want controlled ingress and strict IP allowlists.
- Private endpoints can be fronted by your ALB; Redwoods client certs are optional if you terminate TLS at your edge. We provide a cert rotation cadence and an automation hook for updating endpoint certs (details in the checklist).
- HSM/KMS: Redwood integrates with customer-owned KMIP/HSM for root wrapping. Marissa will share integration docs and the expected operator commands for initial import and key rotation.
- Maintenance & rollback: we recommend a 4-hour canary window (traffic mirrored) followed by a 2-hour cutover window. Full rollback plan is in the runbook (we keep automatic snapshot-based rollback).

Next steps (owners):
1) Ben: prepare the peering IP plan and NAT/EGress configuration for review (action by Fri 09/17).
2) Marissa: publish the on-prem install checklist with HSM/KMS steps and cert rotation examples (action by Mon 09/20).
3) Vivek (me): schedule the initial 2-hour cutover slot and runbook handoff meeting with your ops team for week of 09/20.

Can you confirm your preferred maintenance window (Mon-Fri nights vs. weekend) and the primary contact for cert/key provisioning?

Best,
Vivek
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

---
Attachment(s): redwood-onprem-checklist.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CardioSentry private deployment: on-prem handoff & ops playlist

Vivek / Ben — putting a draft checklist inline so we can iterate before sharing with CardioSentry. Ill attach a versioned spreadsheet too.

-- Draft On‑Prem Install Checklist (v0.1) --
1) Pre-install (owner: Ben)
   - Confirm VPC CIDRs and route table ranges (CardioSentry to provide final list).
   - Confirm whether VPC peering or PrivateLink is preferred and whether transitive routing is allowed.
   - Verify public IP allocations for bootstrap downloads (allowlist our artifacts S3 IPs).

2) Network & Security (owner: Ben)
   - Peering setup steps + expected BGP/static routes. Include one-minute test plan for ping/latency.
   - Firewall rules: open ports 443 (TLS), 22022 (bootstrap ssh), 15000-15010 (internal RPC) — see template.
   - TLS termination plan: ALB vs. Redwood edge; include cert CN and SAN expectations.

3) Secrets & Keys (owner: Marissa)
   - KMS/HSM import: provide required key envelope format and tooling CLI commands.
   - Rotation cadence: recommend 90-day for data keys, yearly for root wrapped by HSM.
   - Ops play: step-by-step restore from snapshot and key rebind test.

4) On‑box configuration (owner: Marissa)
   - Install checklist: packages, kernel params, expected disk layout.
   - Monitoring hooks: prometheus exporters, token-level logging endpoints (to be whitelisted).
   - Backup plan: snapshot and config export frequency (weekly config, daily snapshots).

5) Cutover & Canary (owner: Vivek)
   - Canary window: 4 hours mirrored traffic; success criteria (latency < 90th percentile target, error rate < 0.5%).
   - Rollback: automated revert to prior container images + DB snapshot within 30 minutes.

6) Post-install ops (owner: Grace)
   - 14-day hypercare with 24/7 rotation for first 72 hours.
   - Weekly QBRs for 90 days, then monthly.

Notes: include the firewall-rule-template.txt for baseline rules and the network diagram from CardioSentry.

Marissa
Sr. Implementation Manager, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment(s): redwood-onprem-checklist.xlsx

Subject: CardioSentry private deployment: schedule & agreed next steps

Tom — quick confirmation following our internal alignment. Thanks for the diagram and for confirming a preference for VPC peering. Summary and immediate requests: 

Agreed schedule:
- Friday 2027-09-24 01:00-05:00 PDT: initial canary (4-hour mirrored traffic)
- Saturday 2027-09-25 02:00-04:00 PDT: cutover window (2 hours)

Immediate asks for CardioSentry (please provide by EOD Thu 09/23):
1) Final VPC CIDRs and the contact for your network engineer who will own peering.
2) KMS/HSM operator contact and a test key for import (we will not use production keys for first import).
3) Confirm whether you will terminate TLS at ALB (yes/no) and provide the ALB FQDN.

Public runbook & artifacts were sending now:
- redwood-onprem-checklist.xlsx (v0.2) — includes exact CLI commands for key import and cert rotation examples.
- firewall-rule-template.txt — please align with your SOC for any additional deny rules.
- cardiosentry-network-diagram-v1.pdf (well update after you send CIDRs).

Owners: Ben (peering & NAT), Marissa (install and HSM guidance), Grace (hypercare schedule). Ill run the kickoff call at 09/23 10:00 PDT — invite sent separately.

If any of the proposed windows are problematic, tell us closest alternatives this week and well prioritize. Looking forward to a smooth handoff.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
